title: Local bilinear presheaf pairings extend to sheaf tensor products
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F and G presheaves of O_X-modules with their canonical sheafification units eta_F and eta_G [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], H an O_X-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and U an open of X. Suppose that for each W contained in U there is an O_X(W)-bilinear map b_W:F(W)×G(W)→H(W), and b commutes with every restriction between such opens. There exists a restriction-compatible family of O_X(W)-linear maps d_W:(F^# tensor G^#)(W)→H(W) [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] for W contained in U satisfying d_W(eta_F(x) tensor eta_G(y))=b_W(x,y). No uniqueness, local freeness, or rank hypothesis is required.

proof.text: For j:U→X put V(W)=j(image)(j(preimage)(W)) and K=j_*(H|U). Define beta_W(x,y)=b_V(W)(x|V(W),y|V(W)). The underlying sections K(W) are H(V(W)). Scheme.Hom.app_appIso_inv identifies the scalar action on K(W) with ordinary restriction from O_X(W). The map is therefore bilinear. The two inclusion composites V(Z)→W agree, so the presheaf composition laws and hb give naturality.

The identity map of the structure-ring presheaf is locally injective and locally surjective. Apply existsUnique_bilinear_sheafification_extension to beta and K, obtaining gamma with its naturality and unit equations. Apply tensor_bilinear_universal to gamma to obtain phi:F^# tensor G^#→K.

For W≤U, Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf and Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι give V(W)=W. The restriction-adjunction unit q:H→K at W is restriction along that equality, by restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app, hence bijective because functors preserve isomorphisms. Define e_W=LinearEquiv.ofBijective(q_W) and d_W=e_W.inverse composed with phi_W. Applying injective q_W to the pure tensor equation reduces it to the two universal-property unit equations and hb for V(W)≤W. Applying injective q_Z to naturality reduces it to naturality of q and phi, using e_W(e_W.inverse(z))=z.

lean.statement:
theorem local_bilinear_sheafification_tensor_extension {X : Scheme.{v}}
    (F G : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{v} X.ringCatSheaf.obj) (H : X.Modules)
    (U : X.Opens)
    (b : ∀ W : X.Opens, W ≤ U →
      F.obj (op W) →ₗ[X.presheaf.obj (op W)]
        G.obj (op W) →ₗ[X.presheaf.obj (op W)] H.val.obj (op W))
    (hb : ∀ (W Z : X.Opens) (hW : W ≤ U) (hZW : Z ≤ W) x y,
      b Z (hZW.trans hW) (F.map (homOfLE hZW).op x) (G.map (homOfLE hZW).op y) =
        H.val.map (homOfLE hZW).op (b W hW x y)) :
    let S : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{v} X.ringCatSheaf.obj ⥤ X.Modules :=
      PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{v} (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)
    let η := (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction.{v} (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit
    ∃ d : ∀ W : X.Opens, W ≤ U →
      (S.obj F ⊗ S.obj G).val.obj (op W) →ₗ[X.presheaf.obj (op W)] H.val.obj (op W),
      (∀ W hW x y,
        d W hW (tmulSection ((η.app F).app (op W) x) ((η.app G).app (op W) y)) =
          b W hW x y) ∧
      (∀ (W Z : X.Opens) (hW : W ≤ U) (hZW : Z ≤ W) y,
        H.val.map (homOfLE hZW).op (d W hW y) =
          d Z (hZW.trans hW) ((S.obj F ⊗ S.obj G).val.map (homOfLE hZW).op y))
